title: Wispr raises $280M at $2B valuation to expand beyond AI dictation
summary: Wispr, a startup specializing in AI-powered dictation tools, has secured $280 million in Series B funding at a $2 billion valuation, led by Menlo Ventures. The company plans to use the funds to expand into new areas, including AI-powered meeting note-taking, and improve its speech recognition technology. Wispr also announced a new model, Canto, aimed at reducing dictation error rates from 30% to less than 10%. The startup is scaling its operations globally and exploring new interfaces for human-computer interaction through its Wispr Interface Labs.
key_points: Wispr raised $280 million in Series B funding at a $2 billion valuation, bringing its total funding to $361 million.
The funding round was led by Menlo Ventures, with participation from existing and new investors.
Wispr is expanding beyond dictation into AI-powered meeting note-taking, competing with tools like Granola, Fireflies, and Read AI.
The company launched a new model, Canto, to improve speech recognition accuracy, reducing error rates from 30% to under 10%.
Wispr has scaled its operations in regions like India and the U.K. and partnered with hardware makers like the Oasis ring for silent dictation.
The startup established Wispr Interface Labs to explore new interfaces for human-computer interaction, led by Ariya Rastrow, a former Amazon Alexa team member.
